newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end flat, upswing seen intact.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end flat, upswing seen intact.

text.p: Singapore shares ended virtually unchanged on Wednesday, but dealers said an underlying upswing in prices was still the market's dominant feature. The key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) crept up 0.48 point to 2,220.36 at Wednesday's close leaving the short term upswing intact, said dealers.
"Profit taking will alternate with spells of buying," said one dealer, who said the STII was now safely in a trading range of 2,170 to 2,220.
Trade in local, small-capitalised shares dominated activity which saw 192.81 million units change hands.
Gainers were ahead of losers by 194 to 171 at the close.
Dealers said retail buying of small-capitalised shares followed on the heels of heavy orders in big-capitalised Asian stocks by underweighted foreign fund managers in recent weeks.

Nobel Design, SMB United and Presscrete, all local shares trading at less than Singapore $1.00 (US$0.71), topped the actives list with volumes of 33.52 million, 26 million, and 8.41 million units respectively.
Dealers said they were now waiting for an upswing in a local blue chip, like Singapore Telecom, before seeing another broad move upwards across the STII.
